title: Performance and Re-Renders
description: Understand why React components re-render, how state choices affect performance, and when to use memo, useMemo, and useCallback in real applications.

data.text: React is fast, but not free. Every time state changes, React re-renders the component and its children. In small apps, you will not notice. As your component tree grows, unnecessary re-renders become a real performance problem. Understanding **why** components re-render is the first step to preventing the ones that should not.

items: Calling a state setter from useState or useReducer
A parent component re-rendering (children always re-render unless memoized)
Context value changing, causing all consumers to re-render
A Redux store update causing connected components to re-render
Changing props passed from a parent

data.text: The single most important performance principle in React is this: **minimize the scope of state**. If a state variable is only used by one small component, keep it there. Spreading state high in the tree causes broad re-renders.

State colocation means keeping state as close as possible to where it is used. If an input's value is only needed inside a form field, do not lift it to the page component. Colocated state means fewer components re-render when that value changes.

data.title: Lifting State Too High vs Colocated

data.text: React provides three optimization tools, and each has a specific job. `memo` wraps a component to skip re-renders when its props have not changed. `useMemo` memoizes an expensive calculation. `useCallback` memoizes a function reference so it does not change on every render.

data.title: Preventing Child Re-Renders with memo

data.text: `memo` only helps when props are stable. If you pass inline objects or arrow functions as props, the reference changes every render and `memo` sees them as new props. Wrap handlers with `useCallback` and object literals with `useMemo` to keep references stable.

Do not optimize preemptively. Profile with React DevTools Profiler first. If a component is re-rendering unnecessarily and the Profiler confirms it is slow, then apply `memo` or `useMemo`. Premature optimization adds complexity without measurable benefit.

data.title: Profiler First
data.text: React DevTools Profiler shows you which components rendered, how long they took, and why. Use it to find real bottlenecks before reaching for memoization. Most apps have one or two slow components, not hundreds.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: State colocation is more effective than any optimization hook
memo prevents re-renders when props are unchanged
useMemo and useCallback stabilize references passed to memoized children
Profile before optimizing: measure the actual problem, not a guessed one
